### 2026-11-08: ok so this is my first actual entry talking about the thing that im actually making.

**10h**

ok so this is my first actual entry talking about the thing that im actually making.

the idea for this project comes from another project that i haven't actually made yet but this one seemed cooler and im kinda on PCBs right now so i decided to do this one  (yes, this is the sequel to an imaginary project i have the attention span of a goldfish on cocaine). that project is the magic dice. basically in my digital electronics class we made, and by made i mean soldered a kit imagine actually learning useful things in school lol, that was a randomizer. it had 7 leds and they made a little dice pattern and they switch around when you  press a button and it was cool. so it gave me the idea to make a "magic dice" that is basically just a freeform electronics thing in the shape of a die. you could configure the "sides" and then there would be a tilt sensor and a few capacitors and a 555 timer to step a counter whenever you shook the dice so you could shake it up and then roll it and it would be like a dice but *magic*. kinda like the dice in mario party imagine that.

but that is not what this project is about. i like to memorize cards to exercise my memory. i have like a memory palace and memetic symbols and everything. but, i dont really have time to sit down and look at cards really hard for 2 hours when i get home because i am sleeping, eating, at robotics, at collage, doing this, baking pies, or jumping out of trees. buuut, as far as im concerned learning how to retain and regurgitate pointless repetitive information is the only fucking thing they teach you at school, so im sure they wont mind if i do it there! but there are 2 issues. first of all im not actually sure if im allowed to bring cards to school because gambling or something, and also a deck of cards is a super inconvenient thing to carry around and also whip out during class. i think i need something more... magical. introducing the magic card! its like the magic dice, but a card! just press a button to shuffle the deck, a different button to see the next card. and another button to jump back to the start to test your memory!

so the first thing i needed to figure out was what the display was gonna be. im not going to use a actual digital display or a matrix, because those are LAME, and im also not using a microcontroller for this project, because those are LAME. so, i need a way to represent a card with just 5mm LEDS. my idea was to have 11 "segments" laid out like this:

1.......7

2......8

3..6..9

4......10

5......11

it dosent quite make a perfect playing card pattern, but its pretty close.

those segments would be made of RGB LEDs so they could turn blue (standing in for black) or red.

then, in the block between 1 and 7 there would be 4 little displays that would light up as the suit, and in the block between 4 and 10 there would be 4 little displays as A K Q J for the face cards. its not perfect, but it has charm!

initially i though i was gonna need 3mm leds, so i looked into these 3mm bicolor leds

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/81643e2759dd9c198bf42c05a63c031c3a27939359f1ea8f2577084ce6be94e2.png)

but then i did a little math and actually i can pretty comfortably fit this onto a playing card using 5mm leds!

i found this out by making it in onshape, which sounds weird but i really really really love sketching with constraints i think its so helpful for figuring out where things are going to go in any project.

![2026-11-08-204735_hyprshot](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/431a4c38f81471dd13a3488b65d86a00694cc93e155a46bee7145540da1ecd03.png)

oh also here are some of my paper sketches of the thing.

![IMG_0237](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/4efc3f322b8de2b9ccce183363e89e27bfec3d8cdb609c0592788c43e70ccba1.jpg)

![IMG_0238](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/02f2d8fce390ad15da8804b0267ff76a90a5118e6ab426680f15a5287ce7586c.jpg)

actually i think one of those is me loosing my mind trying to figure out how continuous mass distribution works from base principles, did i say that im scatterbrained already?

also none of those are the final design which still lives in my head  because i figured out what i want to do and thats just how i roll and also this is due in like 2 hours and i have the rest of this entry to write!

so, next issue, how the hell is this gonna work? making a randomized dice roll is easy. just make a fast clock and rely on human error, but how the hell do you shuffle and store the positions of 52 cards? RAM obviously, but remember microcontrollers are lame and if i want to store the positions of 52 cards that is (6 * 52)/4 74ls74 which is like 78 DIP 14 chips also known as way way way to many to fit on a playing card that sounds like gibberish basically i need a better solution. so, i learned about these things called LFSR (Linear Feedback Shift Register), and they quickly because the protagonist of the entire project.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/cadd5beac08b87b914aaff2f3cee9053759a140869bf0c9d84c13409e8268337.png)

basically, you have a shift register, just a bunch of d latches in series, but then you take the xor of 2 bits and feed them back to the input. if you chose the right taps (the bits you xor), the sequence will go through all possible combinations, and it will do it in a convincingly pseudo random order! ITS PERFECT! (well except for one little issue where it skips 000000 because that would make it get stuck there forever yes this will be important and a massive headache later) then all i did was feed the output through a 6 bit XOR hash to remap the cards each shuffle and bada bing bada boom thats the shuffle logic!

![IMG_0233](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/81aca00df298fac9a8d4ae876ba1583f7514849c8f5d9ea0e12a4579c70467dc.jpg)

well actually not quite. there are a few more things. first of all there is another LFSR that stores the seed of the card LFSR so that we can jump back to it when we press the reset button. second of all anything above 51 is an invalid index so we need some way to get rid of those, but thats actually really really hard because of the xor hash. let me introduce you to my extremely stupid solution: just pulse the LFSR again. yep, if we dont like what comes out of the xor hash we just say "do it again" and make the LFSR skip it. its technically entirely deterministic and it is very convenient. so thats the shuffle logic, right?

WRONG, there is one more really really nasty little slimy bug with this setup, can you spot it? remember how i said that the zero index on a LFSR is skipped? well thats ok because we dont need all 64 values, we can just not use it. buuuut that value gets passed through the XOR hash and because it essentially re-maps every value to a different value the missing 0 gets remapped to a random location, which could be within our valid deck range causing us to have a 51 card deck! absolutely horrible.

this one really stumped me for a while, i legit was gonna scrap the XOR hash and make a whole ass binary multiplier, but then i had a incredibly horrific idea. what if we just use a 7 bit LFSR? we only use the top six bits (of yeah i forgot to mention cards are being stored as six bit integers because it was the smallest size 52 fits in) and throw away the bottom one. this makes 000000 a valid index because 0000001 exists. but more issues. 1 the distribution becomes off because 000000 only has 1 valid state as opposed to every other combination which has 2, and 2 its fully possible to get repeating cards now, thats not good! so, this is the second part of my horrible idea, you know how we tell the LFSR to just "do it again" whenever we dont like the number it gives us? what if we do that whenever the first bit is zero? that would make it skip all the repeated cards, giving us a 52 card deck and evening out the distribution! this solution is unbelievably scuffed, but also might work, and im unreasonably proud of it. here is the diagram:

![IMG_0234](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/58a076e24213ab9b6b1ebcfe4220af6ed647b6ba14c77a87307160d90c38f91f.jpg)

and also like the display thats not finished the finished product the skipping logic is wrong for a few reasons i will get to later

ok but detour lets talk about chips. i wanted to use the 74ls series because i have a lot of them and i like them but 2 issues. 1, BIG. they are in DIP package which is like fucking massive and covers the board with impassable through hole walls and would make the front face of the board look really ugly. 2, 5V logic. they only work at 5v and i kinda want to make this at 3.3v because i want ti run this off a coin cell. so i abandoned them and found a new family! screw 74ls, 74LVC is my new best friend! it is basically just like the 74ls series but better! logic levels anywhere between 3v and 6v, tiny SMD SOIC packaging, really cool bonus chips (i found this one that is just 8 d latches that share a clock and it is actually perfect for the LFSRs), and these absolutely adorable tiny little individual gates for when you need a single inverter but dont want to slap down an entire DIP 14 chip! im in love!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/fa1a0e48616ebdb329152986fb6115e01becb6d44f61b2d8703acd115eefff5f.png)

 i haven't fully decided on the exact exact chips im using (like part numbers), but im 100% gonna order all these myself because i want an entire set!

ok anyway combinational logic! i need some gates to turn a 6 bit integer into the signals that go to the 11 individual LEDS (and also the suit and face card indicators but those are basically just 2-4 decoders). thankfully a lot of the LEDS can be wired together because they share the same states, so i only need to make 4 unique circuits. i have the ancient knowledge literally passed on through generations entombed in this book that i got from my old robotics mentor, shout out to KVR your the goat.

![IMG_0236](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/6c72d59f5b89178fd1eb7fd4bc671690df6a85849ad378868798951fd46d7d18.jpg)

and it taught me about grey codes and karnaugh maps and how to optimize and reduce a boolean algebra expression into optimal logic gates!

![IMG_0235](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/SBJjSHTWe8hvDrkl8UXPZsu6tr233Wj5/43e6e1ed79260389906f735b676b76a5e19dad994c901d2072d89bfca3a1eb3b.jpg)

also you know you do to much digital electronics when you dont even need the k maps you can just look at the ones and zeros and go "ah yes this is clearly the xor of bits 2 and 3 and the or of bits 2 and 1" like a fucking psychopath.

and as usual thats not right i messed up handling 1s its just a rough draft :(

anyways thats all the components, well, almost. i still need to figure out how to actually power this whole thing. i was thinking coin cell but there actually isent anywhere for the  SMD holder to go that dosent collide with a led, so i was thinking aaa battery THT pack or like THT coin cell or like tiny lipo i have laying around or like basically im still not sure im gonna figure that out later.
